results.title: Data center GPU price: published rates, dates and sources
results.author: Dora Pruteanu
highlights:
A data center GPU has no single price: an H100 rents at $5.191 per accelerator-hour on AWS Capacity Blocks, $3.99 per GPU-hour on Lambda, and $2.82 on the SemiAnalysis market index (April 2026). This guide separates list, street and contract price and shows which vendors publish none.

...

Key takeaways

- AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks lists an H100 at $5.191 per accelerator-hour in US regions; a B200 is $12.355; AWS has announced new rates from 7 October 2026.
- Lambda rents an on-demand H100 SXM at $3.99 per GPU-hour; 1-Click Clusters run $6.16 at 16 GPUs down to $5.54 at 256.
- H100 1-year rental contracts rose from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026, per SemiAnalysis.
- On-demand H100 capacity has been marked sold out on the SemiAnalysis index from February to April 2026.

## What data center GPUs cost right now

Three published figures answer the question as of 23 September 2026, each from a different price layer. AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML lists the NVIDIA H100 at $5.191 per accelerator-hour in US regions and the B200 at $12.355 per accelerator-hour, with new reservation rates announced effective 7 October 2026 [1]. Lambda lists an on-demand H100 SXM instance at $3.99 per GPU-hour and a B200 SXM6 at $6.69 per GPU-hour [2]. The SemiAnalysis H100 spot-contract composite index, a weighted mean of observed rental prices across the market, stood at $2.82 per GPU-hour in April 2026 [3].

The spread between those numbers is not a contradiction. It reflects three distinct price layers, and a defensible figure names which layer it comes from. The accelerator itself moves the number too: the H100 is no longer the top of the stack, and the B200 and H200 carry different rates on every venue that rents them.

...

- List price: the on-demand rate a provider publishes on its own pricing page, such as Lambda's $3.99 per H100 GPU-hour [2].
- Street price: what market indices observe buyers actually paying. The SemiAnalysis H100 spot-contract composite index is built from hyperscale clouds, neoclouds, marketplaces and rental aggregators, weighted toward hyperscalers.
- Contract price: reserved or committed terms. AWS Capacity Blocks carry a reservation fee plus an operating system fee, and reservation prices are updated regularly with supply and demand.

...

On AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks an H100 rents at $5.191 per accelerator-hour in US regions and a B200 at $12.355, with new rates announced effective 7 October 2026. Lambda lists an on-demand H100 SXM at $3.99 and a B200 SXM6 at $6.69 per GPU-hour. Over the past year, H100 1-year rental contracts rose from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026 per SemiAnalysis, and on-demand H100 capacity was marked sold out on the SemiAnalysis index from February to April 2026.

results.title: AWS reportedly lifts GPU capacity prices again, with a 15% hike flagged for October 7
results.author: Diego Almada Lopez
highlights:
Amazon Web Services may be raising prices on its reserved GPU compute yet again. A post on X claims AWS is lifting reserved compute prices for a fourth quarter, with a 15% increase set to begin October 7.

## What AWS has actually raised in 2026

The increases center on EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML. That product lets customers lock in GPU capacity for machine learning workloads ahead of time.

The first confirmed move came in January 2026. AWS raised Capacity Block prices by approximately 15%, with the hike landing on instances that run NVIDIA H200 GPUs.

A second, larger bump followed on July 1, 2026. That one added roughly 20% to the same GPU capacity service.

The effect shows up clearly on a single machine. After the July change, the H200-based p5e.48xlarge instance went from about $34.61 per hour to about $39 per hour in most regions. In the US West region, the post-July price for that instance reached $49.74 per hour.

The October 7 increase is a different story. The 15% figure comes from the X post, and research findings indicate that number has not been publicly confirmed by AWS.

results.title: AWS GPU Price Increases 2026: What to Do About It
results.author: Kiril Urbonas
highlights:
AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices for ML in January and again on 1 July 2026, so re-run your GPU budget now. Measure utilization per block, split training from inference, price the portable training half at specialist clouds, and renew only blocks you keep above roughly 70% busy. Production inference inside AWS usually stays put.

...

## The rates as of October 2026

These are the per-accelerator-hour Capacity Block rates on AWS's pricing page at the end of October 2026. Every instance has 8 accelerators, so multiply by 8 for the instance-hour.

| Instance | Accelerator | Region shown | Per accelerator-hour | Per instance-hour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | 8 x B300 | US East (N. Virginia) | $16.146 | $129.17 |
| P6-B200 | 8 x B200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $14.208 | $113.66 |
| P5en | 8 x H200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $7.895 | $63.16 |
| P5e | 8 x H200 | US East (Ohio) | $6.866 | $54.93 |
| P5 | 8 x H100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $5.970 | $47.76 |
| P4de | 8 x A100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $2.546 | $20.37 |

When we first wrote this in September, P6-B300 was about $14.04 and P6-B200 about $12.355, so the published rates have moved up roughly another 15% since. The page says prices are updated regularly based on supply and demand, that the next scheduled update is January 2027, and that you pay the rate in effect when you buy, even if the block starts after an update. That last point is the one to act on: if you know you need a block in Q1, buying it before January locks today's rate.

...

### How much does an AWS H100 Capacity Block cost?

As of October 2026, a P5 Capacity Block (8 x H100) lists at $5.970 per accelerator-hour in US East (N. Virginia), about $47.76 per instance-hour. H200-based P5en is $7.895, and Blackwell P6-B200 is $14.208. You pay the rate in effect when you purchase, and AWS's next scheduled price update is January 2027.

results.title: GPU Rental Prices Are Rising Again: What the October 2026 Nebius and AWS Changes Mean for Inference Cost
highlights:
After falling in 2025, H100 rental prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised list prices on 1 October and AWS raised Capacity Blocks on 7 October. Here is what the numbers show and how to plan for them.

...

In short

- GPU rental prices fell in 2025 and are rising in 2026. Nebius raised its H100 on-demand price from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on 1 October 2026.
- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15% in October. AWS on-demand prices did not change.
- One price index put the median on-demand H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October 2026. Hyperscalers charged a median of $10.53 for the same GPU.
- The "price per GPU-hour" you see is a list price. Your real cost per token depends on utilization, and a half-idle GPU costs twice as much per token.
- Plan for price drift: use commitments for steady load, keep workloads portable, and track cost per token, not cost per hour.

...

## What changed in October 2026

Key point

Two large providers raised GPU prices within a week of each other, reversing the 2025 trend.

The Uvik GPU Price Index (captured 7 October 2026) lists the dated events. On 1 October, Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%). It raised H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (+20%). On 7 October, AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15%.

The Nebius pricing page I fetched today matches the new numbers. It lists H100 at $4.50, H200 at $5.40, B200 at $8.50 and B300 at $9.50 per GPU-hour. It also says prices may change at any time.

IntuitionLabs checked AWS on 10 October 2026. The Capacity Blocks rate for P5 (H100) is $5.970 per GPU. In July 2026 it was $5.191 in US regions and $4.720 in other regions. By my calculation from those figures, that is about +15% in the US and about +26.5% elsewhere. AWS says the rates are next scheduled to be updated in January 2027.

Note

Capacity Blocks are reservations, not on-demand. IntuitionLabs warns against using them for cross-provider comparison. AWS on-demand prices did not change in this round.

...

- After falling in 2025, GPU rental prices rose in 2026: on 1 October 2026 Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%) and H200 from $4.50 to $5.40; AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks by about 15% (a reservation product, not on-demand, which did not change; next update scheduled January 2027).
- The Uvik index (19 providers, 87 public on-demand prices) put the median H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October, with a hyperscaler median of $10.53 versus $3.95 for 12 GPU clouds (2.7x). Three-year commitments cut H100 prices by 56% to 57% at the big three.
- Which provider you rent from matters more than the month you rent in.

...

Key point

Even two specialist clouds differ, and list prices are only one input.

The table below uses the Nebius and Runpod pages I fetched today, plus the Uvik medians from 7 October. The Runpod page does not list spot prices or savings-plan rates. Reserved clusters are "contact sales".

| GPU | Uvik median (on-demand) | Nebius on-demand | Runpod Secure Cloud | Runpod Community Cloud |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $4.20 | $4.50 | $3.99 | $2.69 |
| H200 | $5.70 | $5.40 | $5.29 | $3.59 |
| B200 | $8.19 | $8.50 | $7.99 | $5.98 |
| B300 | $9.50 | $9.50 | not listed | not listed |

All prices are per GPU-hour in USD. Community-tier capacity is usually less isolated and less guaranteed, so it is not a like-for-like substitute for the other columns. Check the terms before moving production traffic.

results.title: AI算力需求强劲，亚马逊云业务再次上调GPU服务价格 - XM平台官网 - XM公司专业交易资讯
highlights:
# AI算力需求强劲，亚马逊云业务再次上调GPU服务价格

发布于 2026-11-14 17:52:37浏览 

亚马逊(AMZN.US)旗下的算力上调云计算服务AWS宣布，自7月1日起，需求逊将其机器学习专用EC2 Capacity Blocks的强劲容量预留服务价格上调，涵盖多款搭载英伟达(NVDA.US) GPU的亚马业务实例。这是再次AWS自年初以来再次进行价格调整，表明AI算力需求依然旺盛。算力上调

AWS指出，需求逊此次涨价主要涉及P6-B300、强劲P6-B200、亚马业务P5、再次P5e、算力上调P5en和P4de等实例类型。需求逊其中，强劲 P6-B300和P6-B200使用英伟达的亚马业务Blackwell B300和B200 GPU，而P5系列使用H100和H200 GPU，再次P4系列则配备A100 GPU。

根据最新定价，P6-B300实例的每块GPU小时费用提高至14.04美元，P6-B200涨至12.355美元；P5实例在美国的价格升至5.191美元，非美国地区为4.72美元；P5e和P5en的价格同步上调，而P4de的价格则提高到每块GPU每小时约2.214美元。

AWS还表示，其余服务的价格未做改变，并将根据市场供需情况对EC2 Capacity Blocks机器学习容量预留服务的价格进行定期调整。

分析认为，此次调整再次反映出AI算力资源的供不应求。随着生成式AI、大语言模型以及智能体的迅速发展，对GPU算力的需求持续上升。此外，英伟达的H100、H200及最新的Blackwell系列GPU长期短缺，推动云服务提供商调整租赁价格。

AWS公布的价格还显示，搭载72颗Blackwell GB200 GPU的P6e UltraServer在美国达拉斯地区的每小时租赁费用高达761.9美元，相当于每块GPU每小时约10.58美元。

此外，搭载8颗H100 GPU的P5实例在主要地区的每小时租赁费用约为34.61美元；8颗H200 GPU的P5en实例约为45.77美元；而包含8颗A100 GPU的P4系列实例每小时租赁价格在11.8美元至14.77美元不等。

results.title: AWS rents Nvidia chips for 58 cents an hour, defying GPU ...

AWS lists one of its newest Nvidia GPUs (g7.2xl) at $2.52 an hour. Sign a three-year contract and it drops to 95 cents. Or rent it by the hour with no commitment, what AWS calls spot, for 58 cents in the cheapest zone, 73 on average.

results.title: Cloud GPU Pricing 2026: AWS vs Azure vs GCP Compared
results.author: Simran Sardar
highlights:
The headline rates aren’t comparable. AWS’s $5.19 is prepaid reserved capacity; GCP’s $11.06 and Azure’s $12.29 are metered on-demand. AWS publishes no directly comparable on-demand rate for these families.

...

An H100 GPU-hour costs roughly $5.19 on AWS through prepaid Capacity Blocks, $11.06 on GCP on demand, and $12.29 on Azure on demand. AWS looks far cheaper, but Capacity Blocks are reserved and paid up front rather than metered.

...

| Instance | GPUs | Node price/hr | Per accelerator-hr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| p4d.24xlarge | 8x A100 | $11.80 | $1.48 |
| trn2.48xlarge | 16x Trainium2 | $35.76 | $2.24 |
| p5.48xlarge | 8x H100 | $41.53 | $5.19 |
| p5e.48xlarge | 8x H200 | $47.76 | $5.97 |
| p5en.48xlarge | 8x H200 | $54.92 | $6.87 |
| p6-b200.48xlarge | 8x B200 | $98.84 | $12.36 |
| p6-b300.48xlarge | 8x B300 | $112.32 | $12.36 |

Those are Capacity Blocks rates, which is the detail most comparisons drop. Capacity Blocks are a prepaid capacity product: you reserve a window of instance-hours and pay for it up front. AWS’s own example makes the consequence plain, reserving 192 instance-hours and using only 188 still bills all 192. You are buying a window, not consumption.

Two things sit on top. Operating system charges are separate, so RHEL adds $1.84 per instance-hour. And AWS states that reservation prices update regularly with supply and demand, with the next revision scheduled for October 2026.

results.title: AWS Blackwell GPUs Hit Hyderabad, Beat Azure 40% [2026]
results.author: Daniel Roth
highlights:
AWS ... Blackwell-powered GPU instances ... its ... Pacific ( ... ) ... on September 3, 2026, ... developers ... access to Nvidia’s Blackwell data center silicon, now one step behind Vera Rubin as NVIDIA’s ... architecture, for the first time without routing training jobs through Singapore, Tokyo ... or the US. The move puts Amazon EC2 P6-B200 instances, each packing eight Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, into a region that Microsoft and Google have also been racing to build out over the past year. It also lands at effective pricing that undercuts Azure’s comparable Blackwell instance by roughly 40%, based on published rate cards.

...

According to AWS’s official What’s New announcement, P6-B200 instances became available in the Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) Region starting September 3, 2026, offered in a single configuration: p6-b200.48xlarge. Each instance packs 8 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, 1,440 GB of high-bandwidth HBM3e GPU memory, and 5th-generation Intel Xeon Scalable (“Emerald Rapids”) CPUs delivering 192 vCPUs. AWS pairs that with 2,048 GiB of system RAM, roughly 30 TB of local NVMe storage across eight 3.84 TB drives, and up to 14.4 TB/s of NVLink bandwidth stitching the eight GPUs together for fast intra-node communication, per AWS’s P6 instance family page.

...

Published rate data shows a real spread between the three major clouds on Blackwell B200-class capacity, and it is wide enough to change purchasing decisions for teams running sustained training jobs. In US East (Ohio), AWS lists the 8-GPU p6-b200.48xlarge at an effective $98.84 per hour total, or roughly $12.36 per GPU-hour. Google Cloud’s A4 instances, also built on 8 B200 GPUs, carry an introductory list price around $110 per instance-hour, or about $13.75 per GPU-hour, for short-term reservations, with Spot and committed-use discounts available on top. Azure’s ND GB200 v6 line runs meaningfully higher: a sample ND128isr-NDR-GB200-v6 configuration priced through Azure’s calculator comes to $162.73 per instance-hour in the Australia East region, and a broader AI infrastructure pricing index puts Azure’s average around $27 per GPU-hour, more than double AWS’s rate. Worth a caveat on the AWS number: that $98.84 per hour is AWS’s Capacity Blocks reservation rate, and third-party pricing trackers put on-demand p6-b200.48xlarge higher, around $113.93 per hour (roughly $14.24 per GPU-hour), still well under Azure’s comparable rate.

results.title: AI Cloud Compute Prices Rise Again As GPU Demand Stays Tight
results.author: Tech Help Canada Staff
highlights:
On Sept. 17, Investing.com reported, citing Bloomberg News and an emailed company statement, that Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1. The reported change applies to Nvidia H100, H200, B200, and B300 resources, along with certain CPU and memory resources.

Nebius’s public pricing page, viewed before the reported October change takes effect, listed on-demand rates of $3.85 per GPU-hour for HGX H100, $4.50 for HGX H200, $7.15 for HGX B200, and $7.85 for HGX B300.

## What changed at AWS

AWS’s current EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing page shows how expensive guaranteed high-end AI capacity has become. The page says Capacity Block reservation prices are updated regularly based on supply and demand trends, with the next update scheduled for October 2026.

Current AWS listed rates include $112.32 per hour for a p6-b300.48xlarge instance in several listed regions, or $14.04 per B300 accelerator. For B200 capacity, AWS lists p6-b200.48xlarge at $98.84 per hour, or $12.355 per accelerator, in regions including US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), and US West (Oregon).

Hopper-generation GPU capacity remains costly as well. AWS lists p5e.48xlarge, which uses eight H200 accelerators, at $47.76 per instance-hour, or $5.97 per accelerator. AWS lists p5en.48xlarge in several U.S. regions at $54.92 per instance-hour, or $6.865 per H200 accelerator. These are reservation rates; AWS says operating system charges are billed separately when instances run.

The p5e.48xlarge example shows the scale of the increase. Network World reported in January that the H200-based p5e.48xlarge in US East (Ohio) had increased from $34.608 per instance-hour to $39.799. AWS’s current page lists that same instance type in US East (Ohio) at $47.76 per instance-hour, roughly 38% above the pre-January level reported by Network World.

...

## October is the next pricing checkpoint

Two timing details now stand out. The reported Nebius increases are set to begin Oct. 1, while AWS says current EC2 Capacity Block prices are scheduled to be updated in October 2026.
